source.title: NASA Space Flight Medical Selection, Recertification and Mission Evaluation Standards
source.section: 6. Mission Medical Evaluations for NASA Astronauts Assigned to Spaceflight Missions (Table 8)
source.note: The standard gives these schedules 'for example only', based on a 180-day ISS mission; on the ISS the binding multilateral document is SSP 50667 MED Volume B, which is not public. Demonstration software, not clinical guidance.
source.hardware_note: iss_hardware names come from public NASA material, not from the standard.

routines.title: Health status evaluation
routines.requirement: Crewmembers shall complete periodic health status evaluations in- flight.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on 180-day ISS mission: L+ 14/21 d, L+ 90 d, L+180 d, L+270 d, R- 21/14 d, and ACI.
routines.performed_by: Crew medical officer, reporting to the crew surgeon
iss_hardware: Crew Health Care System (CHeCS) medical kit
steps: Medical history since the last evaluation
Report the findings to the crew surgeon

guide.how: The crew medical officer takes the vital signs of the crew member at rest and asks about symptoms since the last evaluation. Blood tests may be added.
guide.if_abnormal: Repeat the vital sign, record it and tell the crew surgeon. Do not treat on the basis of this evaluation alone.

assumptions: L+180 and L+270 fall on or after landing on a 180-day mission and are dropped
a tolerance of 3 days around L+90 is ours

routines.title: Private medical conference
routines.requirement: Crewmembers shall participate in private medical conferences with a mission assigned FS.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on ISS missions: L+1-7, weekly, pre/post EVA, R- 5 d, daily to R-0 d, and ACI.
routines.performed_by: Crew member and the flight surgeon, on a private link
steps: Review symptoms, sleep, medication and anything the crew member wants to raise
The flight surgeon records the conference

guide.how: A private conversation between the crew member and the flight surgeon; nobody else listens. It is also where the weekly sleep log is discussed.
guide.if_abnormal: The flight surgeon decides the follow-up. On a mission with a long radio delay, record the questions for the next contact.

assumptions: the weekly series starts on L+14 after the first conference in L+1/7
R-0 (landing day) is left out of the daily series

routines.title: In-flight hearing assessment
routines.requirement: Crewmembers will be tested with conventional audiometry before and after flight. Crewmembers shall also conduct pre-flight and in-flight hearing assessments utilizing in-flight hardware.
routines.schedule_text: Example In-flight Schedule based on ISS missions: On or before FD 21, then every 3 months regardless of mission length
routines.performed_by: Crew member, self-administered
iss_hardware: On-Orbit Hearing Assessment software on the station laptop
steps: Put on the attenuating earphones in the quietest module

guide.how: Pure tones of different pitch get quieter until they can no longer be heard; the crew member presses a button each time a tone is heard. The result is the hearing threshold in dB at each frequency.
guide.if_abnormal: Repeat in a quieter module, check that hearing protection is being worn, and tell the crew surgeon. A supplemental test can be requested by the crew member or the crew surgeon.

assumptions: FD21 is mission day 20
'every 3 months' is every 91 days, starting 3 months after FD21, with 7 days of tolerance

routines.title: Specialized ocular assessment (SANS)
routines.requirement: To assess the effects of exposure to the spaceflight environment on ocular health, crewmembers shall undergo specialized eye examinations pre-flight, in-flight, and post-flight.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on 180-day ISS mission: Pre-flight: AME L-21/18 m, L- 9/6 m, In- flight: L+30; L+90; L+180d, L+270 d, R-30;
routines.performed_by: Crew pair, guided from the ground

guide.how: Checks for Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome: fluid shifts towards the head can swell the optic disc and fold the retina. OCT measures the thickness of the retina and optic nerve head; the ultrasound shows the optic nerve sheath.
guide.if_abnormal: Record it and tell the crew surgeon; the standard asks to follow abnormal findings as clinically indicated.

assumptions: L+180 and L+270 are dropped on a 180-day mission
a tolerance of 3 days is ours

routines.title: Bone densitometry (DXA)
routines.requirement: Pre- and post-flight measurements of bone mineral density (BMD) shall be performed.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on ISS 180-day mission: AME L- 21/18 m; L- 180/30 d (as close to launch as feasible), R+ < 30 days, at R+1 year, then as clinically indicated to assess BMD recovery.
routines.performed_by: Ground clinic (there is no DXA on board)
steps: Hip, spine and heel bone mineral density

guide.how: A low-dose X-ray scan measures bone mineral density and lean and fat mass by region. It is the standard terrestrial test; QCT can separate cortical and trabecular bone.
guide.if_abnormal: The standard follows recovery 'as clinically indicated'. Bone loss in flight is estimated by the HealthService from the bed-rest curves, because there is no DXA on board.

assumptions: 'R+ < 30 days' is the window R+0/30
R+1 year has a tolerance of 30 days and is clipped to the end of the simulated mission
AME L-21/18 m is before the simulated mission starts and is dropped

routines.title: Body mass
routines.requirement: Crewmembers shall evaluate body mass periodically while in-flight.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on 180-day ISS mission: L+7, (baseline), then monthly and ACI.
routines.performed_by: Crew member
iss_hardware: SLAMMD (Space Linear Acceleration Mass Measurement Device)
steps: Sit on the device and hold still
The device applies a known force and measures the acceleration

guide.how: Scales do not work without weight, so the device uses Newton's second law: a known force, a measured acceleration, mass = force / acceleration. The value is shared with the weekly dietary questionnaire.
guide.if_abnormal: An unexpected loss of mass triggers a nutritional follow-up; tell the crew surgeon.

assumptions: 'monthly' is every 30 days from L+7

routines.title: Ultrasound imaging (in flight)
routines.requirement: Ultrasound imaging shall be conducted for each crewmember.
routines.schedule_text: other imaging applications may be used on an
routines.performed_by: Crew pair, guided from the ground

guide.how: In flight, ultrasound is used 'as required' (abdomen, heart, vessels), with an expert on the ground guiding the probe.
guide.if_abnormal: The crew surgeon decides the follow-up.

routines.title: Photodocumentation of skin
routines.requirement: The Crew Medical Officer or Crew Surgeon shall document, through photographic imaging, the condition of the crewmember
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on 180-day ISS mission: ACI and R+ 0/1 d.
routines.performed_by: Crew medical officer

guide.how: Photograph the skin finding with a ruler next to it, so its size can be compared over time.
guide.if_abnormal: Send the photographs to the crew surgeon.

assumptions: the post-flight R+0/1 photographs are out of scope of version 1

routines.title: In-flight blood and urine tests
routines.requirement: A clinical laboratory assessment shall be completed for each crewmember before and after flight.
routines.schedule_text: Blood and urine testing in-flight L+180d and ACI.
routines.performed_by: Crew pair

guide.how: Samples are frozen on board and analysed on Earth after the mission.
guide.if_abnormal: Results come back from Earth; the crew surgeon follows them up.

assumptions: L+180 is landing day on a 180-day mission, so nothing is booked in flight

routines.title: Personal radiation dosimetry
routines.requirement: In-flight radiation monitoring shall be performed with crew personal dosimetry according to the specifications in NASA-STD-3001, Volume 2.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on ISS 180-day missions: Ongoing
routines.performed_by: Every crew member wears a dosimeter
steps: Wear the personal dosimeter at all times

guide.how: Continuous: the dosimeter records the dose and type of ionizing radiation received.
guide.if_abnormal: Exposure limits are set in NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2; during a solar particle event the crew moves to the shielded area.

routines.title: Jugular vein ultrasound (DVT screening)
routines.requirement: Every crewmember shall be screened for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and flow anomalies of the internal jugular veins.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on 180-day ISS mission: L-12/3 m, L+30 days; L+60 days; R-42 days, R+0/45d, ACI.
routines.performed_by: Crew pair, with teleguidance or autonomously with just-in-time training
steps: Duplex ultrasound of both internal jugular veins
Save the images for the ground

guide.how: The probe on the neck shows the vein and the speed and direction of the blood. A healthy vein collapses when pressed; one with a clot does not. Left jugular thrombosis has been found in flight without symptoms.
guide.if_abnormal: Tell the crew surgeon at once; do not wait for the next routine scan.

assumptions: a tolerance of 3 days is ours

routines.title: Functional fitness assessment
routines.requirement: Each crewmember shall complete a series of tests designed to establish functional fitness before and after flight.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on ISS missions: AME L-9/6 m; L-90/30 d, R+5/7 d, R+30 d.
routines.performed_by: Ground strength and conditioning team
equipment: functional tests (sit and reach, push-ups, pull-ups, leg press, agility, hand grip)

guide.how: In this demo the isokinetic dynamometer readings stand in for the functional fitness battery.
guide.if_abnormal: Guides post-flight rehabilitation; the HealthService compares each test with the pre-flight reference.

assumptions: the dynamometer stands in for the whole functional fitness battery
AME L-9/6 m is before the simulated mission starts and is dropped

routines.title: On-orbit strength monitoring
routines.requirement: Each crewmember shall undergo strength and conditioning monitoring during flight.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on 180-day ISS mission: Strength and conditioning monitoring - Recurrent in-flight; L+14 days (NET 3rd session) and then at least every 30 days thereafter.
routines.performed_by: Crew member; reviewed by ground exercise specialists
steps: Strength test on the resistive device
Downlink the exercise data and video

guide.how: Exercise data and video are reviewed on the ground and the crew member gets individual recommendations. The demo uses dynamometer torque as the strength measure.
guide.if_abnormal: The HealthService decides if a loss is beyond expected; the Planner then books a retest or a review.

assumptions: 'at least every 30 days' is booked every 30 days with 3 days of tolerance

routines.title: Aerobic capacity test (VO2peak)
routines.requirement: Each crewmember shall complete tests to assess aerobic functional capacity and exercise induced arrhythmias before flight, periodically in-flight, and post-flight.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on ISS missions: AME L-12 m, L-90/30 d, FD14, FD75, FD 165, FD 255, R-14 d, R+ 5 d, R+ 30 d, ACI.
routines.performed_by: Crew member, monitored from the ground
steps: Upright cycling with an incremental load, same protocol before, during and after flight

guide.how: The load goes up step by step until the crew member cannot continue; the test gives the maximum heart rate and the peak oxygen uptake.
guide.if_abnormal: NASA-STD-3001 asks to keep VO2max at or above 80% of the pre-mission value; the HealthService flags a loss and the Planner books a retest or a review.

assumptions: FD N is mission day N - 1
AME L-12 m is before the simulated mission starts and is dropped
FD255 is after landing on a 180-day mission and is dropped

routines.title: Pre- and post-EVA medical exam
routines.requirement: All EVAs shall be preceded and followed by an assessment of medical fitness by the Crew Surgeon.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on ISS missions: Pre- and Post-EVA.
routines.performed_by: Crew surgeon, with the crew medical officer on board
steps: Skin and extremity exam, hands and nails included
Before: confirm fitness for the spacewalk; after: check for decompression symptoms and injuries

guide.how: Within 48 hours before putting on the suit and 24 hours after taking it off.
guide.if_abnormal: Before: the crew surgeon decides if the spacewalk goes ahead. After: report any symptom of decompression sickness at once.

routines.title: EVA monitoring
routines.requirement: Crewmembers shall undergo EVA monitoring as per the requirements in NASA-STD-3001, Volume 2.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on ISS missions: During EVA.
routines.performed_by: Automatic, from the spacesuit telemetry
equipment: suit pressure, CO2 and O2 sensors
steps: O2 tank pressure and metabolic rate

guide.how: Telemetry from the suit reaches the flight director during the whole spacewalk.
guide.if_abnormal: The EVA flight director acts in real time.

routines.title: Private psychological conference
routines.requirement: Crewmembers shall participate in a private psychological conference, performed by a specialist, according to the specifications and schedule described below.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on 180-day ISS mission: In-flight every 14 days, and ACI.
routines.performed_by: Crew member and a behavioral health specialist, on a private link
steps: Crew dynamics and interactions with the ground

guide.how: A private conversation about mood, performance, crew dynamics and ground-crew interactions.
guide.if_abnormal: The specialist decides the follow-up with the crew surgeon.

assumptions: the series starts on L+14

routines.title: Cognitive assessment
routines.requirement: Crewmembers shall undergo a cognitive assessment before, during, and after flight.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on 180-day ISS mission: L- 390 d, L- 330 d, L- 270 d, L- 210 d, L- 150 d, L- 90 d, In-flight: 1/month and as indicated, Post-flight: R+ 30 d, and ACI.
routines.performed_by: Crew member, on the station laptop
equipment: cognitive test battery on a laptop

guide.how: About 30 minutes of computer tests; each result is compared with the crew member's own pre-flight baseline.
guide.if_abnormal: Repeat after rest and tell the crew surgeon, especially after a head injury, decompression sickness or toxic exposure.

assumptions: '1/month' is every 30 days from L+30

routines.title: Vitamin D supplement
routines.requirement: Crewmembers shall be evaluated and treated prior to a long-duration mission.
routines.schedule_text: Example Schedule based on ISS 180-day missions: ACI daily or once/week.
routines.performed_by: Crew member
equipment: vitamin D3 from the on-board pharmacy
steps: Take the weekly maintenance dose (5000 I.U. vitamin D3) or the dose the crew surgeon prescribed

guide.how: There is no sunlight inside the vehicle. Maintenance dose: 1,000 I.U. daily or 5,000 I.U. once a week; desired 25-OH vitamin D range 35-90 ng/ml.
guide.if_abnormal: Dosing for low pre-flight levels is set by the crew surgeon, following the dosing table in the NASA standard.

assumptions: booked as the weekly maintenance dose; a daily dose is equally valid

routines.title: Dietary questionnaire
routines.requirement: Crewmembers shall undergo nutritional assessment testing according to the specifications and schedule described below.
routines.schedule_text: Standard dietary assessment questionnaire
routines.performed_by: Crew member
equipment: dietary questionnaire on a laptop or tablet
steps: Record what and how much was eaten

guide.how: Estimates energy, protein, calcium and other nutrient intake from the week's food.
guide.if_abnormal: Unexpected loss of mass, change in energy expenditure or malaise calls for more follow-up and possibly a diet prescription.

assumptions: the questionnaire is booked every 7 days from L+7

routines.title: Sleep log
routines.requirement: Each crewmember shall provide a daily assessment of sleep quality and quantity: for a 2-week pre-flight period, 1 week pre-launch, weekly in-flight via Private Medical Conference, and 1-week post-flight to supply daily sleep data to the crewmember and Crew Surgeon.
routines.schedule_text: L-7 days continuously until R+7 days.
routines.performed_by: The watch logs the hours; the crew member rates the night on waking

guide.how: Rate the night on waking; an actigraphy watch can add the times actually asleep. The data is discussed at the weekly private medical conference.
guide.if_abnormal: Repeated short or poor sleep is discussed with the crew surgeon; sleep medication must have been tested on the ground before flight.

assumptions: one daily item with half a day of tolerance
closed by the watch's nightly sleep report (sleep_hours), docs/wearable.md
